## We do big things. This isn’t just our past — it’s our future. And I want to build that future together.
Amy Klobuchar is running for governor, with her running mate Ben Schierer, because Minnesotans deserve to have their work recognized and rewarded. She’s running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first house; for every parent who wants a better world for their kids; for everyone who wants affordable health care. As Governor, Amy will focus on lowering costs for families, getting results for Minnesotans, rooting out fraud, and making the government accountable to the people of our state.
## Meet Amy
Amy Klobuchar has always been guided by the values she learned growing up in Minnesota — the granddaughter of an iron ore miner and the daughter of a newspaperman and a second-grade teacher. She’s never shied away from taking on tough fights, whether that’s working to guarantee 48-hour hospital stays for new moms and babies, prosecuting fraud and corruption when she ran the biggest prosecutor’s office in the state, or taking on pharmaceutical companies, Big Tech, and Trump’s tariffs in the Senate. She’s been ranked #1 for authoring bipartisan bills and #3 for passing bills into law. Amy has worked to deliver results for Minnesotans, and that’s exactly what she’ll do as Governor.

pages.title: Priorities - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Amy Klobuchar is running for governor because Minnesotans deserve to have their work recognized and rewarded.
She’s running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first house. For every parent who wants a better world for their kids. For everyone who wants affordable health care. For every worker looking for a good job in a cutting-edge industry. For every student, farmer, dreamer, and builder.
Because Minnesota built this nation. We invented everything from the pacemaker to the Post-it Note. We do big things. That’s not just our past — it’s our future.
Amy Klobuchar will carry this forward as Governor, working to lower costs for families, make the government accountable, root out fraud, and get results for Minnesotans.
## Lower Costs for Minnesotans
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work to lower costs that have been going through the roof across the country — essentials like health care, housing, child care, and utility bills. She’ll build on her years of fighting — and beating — Big Pharma to lower prescription drug prices for Minnesotans. She’ll take action to build more homes for Minnesotans, supporting first-time homebuyers, renters, and growing families who need more space. She’ll work with child care providers, employers, and schools to expand access to child care. And she’ll hold the line on utility bills by modernizing Minnesota’s power grid and adding more affordable, renewable energy.
## Make Government Accountable and Root out Fraud
We need a government that can carry its weight and match your drive and ambition. Amy Klobuchar intends to transform our state government to be innovative , effective , and accountable . That starts by rooting out fraud and making sure the money coming out of your paycheck is not misspent. It means modern technology that delivers results fast. It means making it easy to start a business and bring good-paying jobs to Minnesota. It means turning the page on a bureaucracy that leaves people dreading having to jump through hoops to get a permit or start a business. Amy Klobuchar will take on our biggest challenges.
## Prepare Minnesota’s Workforce for the Future
Amy Klobuchar knows there are many paths to success. As Governor, she’ll make sure Minnesotans can get the skills they need to build a good life here at home. She’ll build real on-ramps to good jobs, doubling apprenticeships and workforce training in the trades, health care, public safety, and emerging industries. She’ll raise academic achievement with evidence-based curriculum, tutoring to help kids catch up, and a focus on reading and math skills in elementary classrooms. And she’ll open doors to college and credentials, building partnerships between employers and colleges, expanding three-year degrees, and helping middle and high school students get a head start. Because anybody willing to work should have a path to success.
## Take on Crime and Support Public Safety
Amy Klobuchar ran the biggest prosecutor’s office in Minnesota for eight years as Hennepin County Attorney, where she made combating violent crime a top priority. She knows firsthand the vital role law enforcement and public safety officers play in keeping Minnesotans safe – and the importance of giving them the resources they need to do their jobs. In the Senate, Klobuchar has worked across party lines to increase support for local law enforcement and combat fraud, human trafficking, and the fentanyl epidemic. As Governor, she will take on organized crime and gang violence, assist local police departments to hire and retain more officers, provide Minnesota law enforcement with the resources they need to do their jobs, and more.
## Expand Minnesota’s Rural and Agricultural Economy
Amy Klobuchar knows one-size-fits-all solutions don’t work for rural communities. She and her running mate, former Fergus Falls Mayor Ben Schierer, will expand Minnesota’s rural economy by working with businesses and farmers to grow and produce more products, find new markets, and export to the world. They will work with the private sector to build more homes, support rural hospitals, increase access to child care, and create new pathways to the workforce. They’ll modernize rural broadband and infrastructure, and strengthen the farm safety net. Together, they will make sure Minnesotans can live, work, and raise a family anywhere in Minnesota — because kids who grow up in rural Minnesota should be able to stay in rural Minnesota.
## Support Conservation and Outdoor Recreation
Amy Klobuchar is committed to preserving Minnesota’s natural resources and protecting the environment. As Governor, she will protect Minnesota’s natural resources, from lakes and wetlands to forests and farmland. She will promote strategies that protect public lands and wildlife habitat, preserve farmland, reduce fires and flooding, and keep our state’s air and water clean. She knows we all share a responsibility to pass on the Minnesota way of life to future generations through conservation and smart policies that allow outdoor recreation, fishing, and hunting to thrive.
## Amy Klobuchar wants to build this future together. She was ranked number one for authoring bipartisan bills and number three for passing bills into law. She believes in getting things done. No excuses.

pages.title: Make Health Care More Affordable and Accessible - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Make Health Care More Affordable and Accessible
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will keep fighting to lower health care costs so families can afford to get the care they need.
Watch in a new tab
“While the Trump administration’s lack of action on health care tax credits have raised premiums for Minnesotans and put our hospitals at risk, as Governor I’ll lower costs.
“Before I ever held office, I took on the insurance companies for kicking new moms out of the hospital just 24 hours after giving birth – and won.
In the Senate, I took on the pharmaceutical companies by leading the fight to let Medicare negotiate lower prescription drug prices – and won.
As Governor, I’ll reduce premiums, lower prescription drug costs, and protect access to care at our hospitals and clinics. These are fights I know how to win.”
Amy Klobuchar has long fought to make health care more affordable and accessible. She got involved in politics after the birth of her and John’s daughter, Abigail, who couldn’t swallow when she was born. Even though Abigail was in intensive care, Klobuchar was discharged from the hospital after just 24 hours because of insurance rules. As a mom who had never held political office, she became the leading advocate for the successful passage of one of the first laws in the country guaranteeing 48-hour hospital stays for new moms and their babies.
Amy Klobuchar has been taking on unfair and costly health care practices ever since. As our U.S. Senator, she led the law that ended the nearly 20-year sweetheart deal that banned Medicare from negotiating lower prescription drug prices – a ban that raised prices at the expense of seniors and taxpayers. That provision has been used by both the Biden and Trump administrations to negotiate lower prescription drug prices, which is estimated to save $12 billion for Medicare beneficiaries and the government. She’s also fought the anti-competitive practices that keep affordable generics off pharmacy shelves, passed landmark bipartisan laws to combat the opioid epidemic, and taken on insurance companies over the paperwork games that delay care. She voted for the Affordable Care Act and supported the public option as well as the premium tax credits. And she secured federal research investments that fuel our hospitals and universities while leading the successful fight to repeal the medical device tax that threatened thousands of Minnesota jobs.
Klobuchar is one of the leaders in the Senate who has taken on the Trump administration’s recent cuts to health care. Because of the administration’s actions, what families pay for health insurance on the individual market is projected to more than double and more than 6 million Americans have already lost their insurance, with more national Medicaid cuts coming next year. These actions threaten to close hundreds of rural hospitals, community health centers, and nursing homes across the country.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will keep fighting to lower health care costs so families can afford to get the care they need. She’ll work to negotiate lower prescription drug prices. She’ll hold companies accountable and ensure what they charge actually reflects the cost of care. She’ll improve access to care by strengthening hospitals and clinics, especially in rural areas, expanding our health care workforce, and modernizing IT systems. She will always protect a woman’s right to make her own health care decisions.
Minnesota is an international hub for innovative care, cures, and medical technology. Klobuchar will expand on and strengthen our state’s medical innovation. She’ll partner with our world-class hospitals and research institutions to advance the future of medicine in Minnesota, build a statewide innovation network that turns discoveries into companies and jobs, drive medical innovation that increases competition and expands patient choice, and prepare our workforce for the health care careers of the future.
- Lower health care costs by bringing down premiums to deliver more value and leveraging the state’s purchasing power to lower prescription drug costs
- Protect access to care by strengthening rural health care, safety-net hospitals and clinics, and health systems.
- Support medical innovation and our health care workforce – build on our state’s position as an international hub for cures, treatments, and technology by expanding and preparing our health care workforce and supporting new innovation.
## 1. Lower Health Care Costs
Across the country, including in Minnesota, families are facing rising health insurance premiums because of the Trump administration’s refusal to extend the health care tax credits, with out-of-pocket premiums increasing 58% nationally on the individual market last year. Deductibles have risen even more, and prescription drug prices continue to skyrocket. Instead of lowering costs, the Trump administration just made the largest health care cuts in American history, causing millions of Americans to lose their coverage.
As our U.S. Senator, Amy Klobuchar has fought to lower health care costs by leading the fight for the law that finally allowed Medicare to negotiate lower prescription drug prices, and fighting anti-competitive practices that keep affordable generics off pharmacy shelves and raise prices for prescription drugs. As Governor, she will build on that work to lower prescription drug costs by expanding state bulk purchasing of drugs and prioritizing lower-cost generics and biosimilars. Klobuchar will also bring down premiums, strengthen reinsurance to hold down premiums, support small businesses in covering their employees, and help Minnesotans without employer coverage afford insurance.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will also take on the complicated and outdated systems that are driving up costs, making it difficult to access care, and creating opportunities for fraud. She will have zero tolerance for Medicaid fraud and will root it out and stop it before it starts. She’ll make it easier to access care by simplifying forms for billing, insurance, hospital assistance, and prior authorizations, and launch a “What’s it Cost?” tool to bring more transparency to the cost of medical care so families can compare the cost of procedures before they set foot in a clinic, helping lower premiums in the process. And she will work to rein in corporate health care costs by ensuring pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) pass along savings – no more hidden markups, and no more pocketing rebates that belong to consumers.
## Reduce health care premiums.
- Reduce premiums to deliver immediate cost relief and value for Minnesota families, small business owners, farmers, contractors, and others without employer coverage. Many Americans have not been able to afford their health insurance since the Trump administration let the premium tax credit expire. To limit increases in Minnesota, Klobuchar will direct the Minnesota Department of Commerce to weigh affordability as a factor in the rate review process and deny excessive hikes. She’ll also extend and strengthen Minnesota’s bipartisan reinsurance program, which for nearly a decade has helped Minnesotans who purchase their own insurance, by securing renewal of the waiver before it expires at the end of 2027.
- Lower premiums on MNsure. When the Trump administration let the enhanced premium tax credit expire, families’ costs jumped overnight, and Americans buying their own insurance were hit hard. As Governor, Klobuchar will continue advocating for an extension of the federal premium tax credits and, if there is no federal action, she will work to create a state tax credit, delivered through MNsure, targeted at the small business owners, self-employed workers, and farmers hit hardest by the federal tax credit expiration.
- Give small businesses a tax credit to help cover their employees’ health insurance. Small businesses want to do right by their workers but are being priced out of offering coverage. As Governor, Klobuchar will create a per-employee state tax credit for small employers who fund their workers’ health coverage, so Main Street can compete with big companies for talent without going broke doing it.
Increase transparency and reform government.
- Launch a “What’s it Cost?” tool so families can see the price of care before they get it. Klobuchar’s administration will launch a tool so families can compare the cost of procedures – like an MRI, a surgery, or childbirth – before they ever set foot in a clinic, the same way they shop for any other service.
- Simplify paperwork by promoting a “One-Form” system for health insurance. Klobuchar will modernize the health care system by moving toward a “one-form” standard for billing, insurance, hospital assistance, and prior authorizations. She will require insurers and providers to use a standardized format to eliminate the redundant paperwork shuffle between patients, providers, and insurance companies, so doctors spend more time with patients and patients stop facing weeks of delay and months of confusion over medical bills. Read Klobuchar’s full plan to transform state government at AmyKlobuchar.com/accountable .
- Zero tolerance for health care fraud – root it out and stop fraud before it starts. Klobuchar will transform state government across health programs so every health care dollar goes to care, not to services not delivered. Her administration will screen providers before they receive funding against a state “Do Not Pay” database; freeze suspicious payments before money goes out the door; prosecute fraud to the fullest extent of the law; use modern payment systems to catch billing anomalies in real time; and implement the recently passed bipartisan legislation to stand up the independent Office of Inspector General. Read Klobuchar’s full plan to transform state government at AmyKlobuchar.com/accountable .
Lower prescription drug costs.
- Expand state bulk purchasing of prescription drugs. Building on Klobuchar’s Senate leadership that finally removed the Big Pharma sweetheart deal and allowed Medicare to negotiate lower drug prices, she will use the full authority of the executive branch to expand Minnesota’s bulk-purchasing of prescription drugs. Her administration will harness the Minnesota Multistate Contracting Alliance for Pharmacy (MMCAP), the largest multistate public purchasing pool in the nation, to consolidate pharmaceutical buying across state agencies and programs, and align any state employee plans alongside it.
- Make lower-cost generics and biosimilars more available. Building on Klobuchar’s work in the Senate to expand competition through generics and biosimilars, she will make lower-cost alternatives automatically available for prescription drugs across state programs as well as other lower-cost options and referrals for consumers.
- Convene a Minnesota employer purchasing coalition. Klobuchar will convene a coalition of large public and private Minnesota employers to align on purchasing high-cost drugs, share strategies for fair contracting with PBMs and other industry middlemen, and accelerate use of lower-cost equivalent drugs. She will help Minnesota employers work together to negotiate fair prices from national PBMs.
- End predatory practices by pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs). Klobuchar will end practices that don’t pass along savings from discounts and conduct that steers patients to PBM-owned pharmacies, raising costs for Minnesotans.
## 2. Protect Access to Care
Several hospitals and clinics across Minnesota – many of them in rural areas – are at heightened risk of closing or reducing services due in part to the Trump administration’s national Medicaid cuts in the Big Beautiful Bill. After these cuts fully kick in, more than 140,000 Minnesotans could lose their health coverage.
Amy Klobuchar led the fight against these federal cuts in the Senate and will protect access to health care as Governor, both by advocating for funding and by supporting hospitals and clinics in modernizing facilities and upgrading infrastructure. And she’ll provide support for Minnesotans who qualify for Medicaid so red tape and paperwork don’t take away their coverage, while modernizing the health systems Minnesotans rely on so applying for and keeping coverage is streamlined and seamless.
Klobuchar will also stand up for reproductive freedom, expand access to mental health services, and provide resources for addiction.
Protect coverage from federal cuts and improve the health care system.
- Strengthen safety net and rural health care – hospitals, clinics, EMS, and pharmacies – and help Minnesotans retain coverage. Klobuchar will keep care close to home both in the Metro and in Greater Minnesota by supporting the hospitals and clinics families rely on. She will provide targeted grants to modernize facilities and upgrade aging infrastructure, protect the 340B discounts that keep rural and safety net hospitals open, and provide funding for rural emergency medical services – including for rapid-response emergency vehicles statewide so help comes fast, no matter your ZIP code. She will advocate for restoring the Medicaid funding cuts in the Big Beautiful Bill and use every available data source to make sure Minnesotans retain coverage.
- Modernize the systems Minnesotans rely on. Klobuchar will modernize government technology to deliver results faster. That includes completing the state health insurance portal upgrades, expanding data-driven automatic renewals, and moving toward one-stop enrollment, so applying for and keeping coverage is streamlined and seamless. Read Klobuchar’s full plan to transform state government at AmyKlobuchar.com/accountable .
## Protect access to care.
- Put primary care first . Everyone does better, and the whole system costs less, when Minnesotans have a regular primary care provider – whether that’s a doctor, registered nurse, clinician, community health worker, social worker, or pharmacist – who knows them, catches problems early, and coordinates their care. As Governor, Klobuchar will make primary care the foundation of Minnesota health care. She will continue rewarding providers for getting and keeping people healthy from the start, rather than waiting for an emergency.
- Expand telehealth services . Klobuchar will guarantee that care delivered by telehealth is covered and paid at the same rate as in-person care, for all services and all plans, and make coverage of audio-only visits permanent, so seniors and rural Minnesotans without reliable broadband aren’t left behind. Building on her leadership on broadband in the Senate, she will finish the job on universal broadband and a stronger statewide digital health framework so residents in every ZIP code can see specialists from home.
- Support our veterans’ health care . Klobuchar will work with federal authorities and County Veterans Service Officers to cut through red tape and make sure Minnesota veterans can access the full Veteran Affairs (VA) health care and mental health services they’ve earned. Her administration will also join the VA’s Governor’s Challenge to strengthen veteran suicide prevention across the state.
- Expand mental health access across Minnesota. Klobuchar will work to restore and expand the school-linked mental health grants so kids and their parents can get help in school. She will build the mental health workforce, including dedicated rural mental health counselors and social workers. Her goal will be to add psychiatric bed capacity, with a specific focus on kids, building on the 2025 bonding investment. She will direct the Commerce Department to enforce equal coverage for mental and physical health, so insurance covers mental health and addiction care like the health care it is. And she will work to fully fund Minnesota’s mobile crisis response so that in a mental health emergency, help comes where it is needed.
- Build and expand on Minnesota’s leading work on addiction. Building on Klobuchar’s work as county attorney and in the Senate, she will expand access to evidence-based drug and alcohol treatment and prevention. As U.S. Senator and as Hennepin County Attorney, she has long supported drug courts, as well as therapies, treatment, prevention, and research into new and effective treatment options. She will ensure every opioid settlement dollar is used for treatment and prevention, expand rural treatment capacity, and partner with counties, towns, and Tribal Nations.
- Protect reproductive freedom. Klobuchar will protect the reproductive rights codified in state law by the PRO Act.
## 3. Support Medical Innovation and Our Health Care Workforce
Minnesota does big things – and nowhere is that more true than in medicine. We are home to leading hospitals, world-class research universities, and one of the largest medical technology hubs in the world. Minnesota has always been where the future of medicine is built – from the first successful open-heart surgery at the University of Minnesota to the first wearable battery-powered pacemaker, and from pioneering work in personalized medicine and mapping the human genome at the Mayo Clinic and other health institutions to the breakthroughs being developed in our labs today. But other states and countries are competing aggressively for the jobs, research dollars, and talent that Minnesota has long led on, and we can’t take that leadership for granted.
In the Senate, Amy Klobuchar led the successful fight to repeal the medical device tax that threatened thousands of Minnesota medtech jobs, and she has championed the federal research investments that fuel our hospitals and universities. She has fought recent Trump administration cuts to National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding and research grants, which have put cancer trials and cures at risk. As Governor, she will partner with our world-class hospitals and research institutions to keep building the future of medicine here in Minnesota, create a statewide innovation network that turns discoveries into companies and jobs, drive medical innovation that increases competition and expands patient choice, and prepare our workforce for the health care careers of the future.
Klobuchar also knows we need to expand our health care workforce, including doctors, nurses, clinicians, medical technicians, pharmacists, dental hygienists and dentists, so Minnesotans don’t have to drive two hours or wait two months to get care. She’ll do this by recruiting and training medical professionals, expanding health care pipelines, and supporting primary care providers. Klobuchar’s full plan to recruit, train, and retain Minnesota’s workforce, including the health care sector, is available at AmyKlobuchar.com/workforce .
## Support Minnesota’s medical innovation.
- Build on and expand Minnesota’s role in the next generation of treatment and cures , including our long support of research, the mapping of the human genome, and responsible use of technology. The Trump administration has cut NIH funding and canceled research grants, putting cancer trials and cures at risk. Klobuchar will incentivize and expand partnerships with research institutions, companies, philanthropies, and universities to develop groundbreaking cures. This means keeping world-class research, clinical trials, and the jobs that come with them here in Minnesota, with a dedicated commitment to diseases including cancer, Alzheimer’s, and historically under-emphasized women’s health research, from mammograms to menopause.
- Launch a Minnesota Innovation Network. Minnesota’s next generation of cures and treatments will come from connecting researchers, entrepreneurs, and health systems, so a discovery made in a Rochester or Twin Cities lab or a rural startup becomes a treatment, a company, and Minnesota jobs. As Governor, Klobuchar will build a coordinated statewide system that connects Minnesota businesses to universities, research centers, and incubators with local innovation hubs focused on health care along with advanced manufacturing, energy, and agriculture. Klobuchar’s administration will pool resources and use public-private financing to bring new treatments from the lab to the market faster and connect innovators with employers.
Support Minnesota’s health care workforce.
- Launch Minnesota Health Care Future to expand our health care workforce. Minnesota must recruit and train doctors, nurses, and medical technicians. Klobuchar’s administration will work with the University of Minnesota and the state college system, as well as Minnesota employers and unions, to develop specialized recruitment campaigns and training pathways to encourage medical professionals to live and work in the Minnesota communities that need them most. One of many examples is the University of Minnesota’s NXT GEN MED three-year degree program in Rochester.
- Expand health care pipelines. Klobuchar’s administration will work to waive initial application fees for nurses, doctors, and med techs. Klobuchar will work to expand alternative pathways and streamline credentialing so graduates in other fields can transition into classrooms and clinics.
- Strengthen registered apprenticeships to additional industries like biotech and health care. Klobuchar is committed to working with the private and public sectors, as well as unions, to add 10,000 apprenticeship and skills training opportunities, including for health care workers. Building on the success of apprenticeships in the trades, she will bring the Minnesota Apprenticeship Initiative to additional industries like health care and biotech. She will work with employers and schools to connect high school students directly to emerging and high-demand careers such as nursing.
- Expand the primary care and maternal care workforce. Klobuchar will work with employers and schools to train and recruit the primary care providers Minnesota needs – including family doctors, nurses, dentists, and community health workers – with a focus on the communities that have gone without them, so that seeing a primary care provider doesn’t mean a three-month wait or a three-hour drive. Our state should expand access to OB-GYNs, midwives, and other maternal health providers, and work to end the disparities that leave Black mothers roughly three times, and Native mothers more than four times, as likely to die from pregnancy-related causes.
- Create partnerships between local employers, community colleges, and public and private colleges and universities, and advance Minnesota’s STEM education. Klobuchar will create partnerships between community colleges and local employers who are competing in the global economy to design curricula and credentials for high-demand jobs that exist right now, in fields such as health care, so training aligns directly with local hiring needs. She will work with our world-class tech and medical industries to expand science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education, with mentorships, internships, and curriculum aligned to the jobs being created in Minnesota.

pages.text:
## Lower Housing Costs for Minnesotans
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work to lower costs that have been going through the roof across the country — essentials like housing, child care, and health care.
Watch in a new tab
“Housing is the key to unlocking opportunity and the foundation for our lives.
“You can’t start a family if you can’t afford a home for them. You can’t accept a job in a town you can’t afford to live in. And you can’t start a new business or save for retirement if your rent is eating up your paycheck.
We must take action to put buying a home and lower rents within reach for more people.”
## A plan to lower housing costs by building more homes and stopping rip-offs.
- Build more homes, faster.
- More housing in rural communities.
- Make owning a manufactured home more affordable.
- Support renters and stop rip-offs.
- Help Minnesotans buy homes and afford rent.
- Prevent and reduce homelessness.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work every day to lower costs and make life more affordable for Minnesota families. That starts with housing.
Housing is the biggest expense most families face every month, and Minnesotans deserve to have access to homes they can afford.
This affects people across our state – young and old, urban, suburban, and rural. The median age of a first-time buyer in Minnesota has risen to 40 and half of Minnesota renters now spend more than 30% of their paycheck on housing.
Amy Klobuchar will lower housing costs by putting us on a path to end our housing shortage by building 100,000 homes, including in rural communities; supporting manufactured homeowners; ending rip-offs by out-of-state companies; and making it easier for Minnesotans to buy homes ; and addressing homelessness.
## 1. Build More Homes, Faster
Minnesota has a shortage of approximately 100,000 homes. The fastest way to lower housing costs is to build and rehabilitate homes to reduce that shortage. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar is committed to filling the housing gap by putting us on a path to build at least 100,000 homes, condos, and apartments.
She’ll do that by reforming permitting, cutting red tape, and removing the delays and fees that drive up costs. Amy Klobuchar is fighting so builders can build and Minnesotans have homes they can afford. And now that the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act – which Klobuchar shaped and which includes her Housing Supply and Affordability Act – is law, she will work to ensure Minnesota receives resources from new federal housing programs .
## Reform permitting and set deadlines that the government meets, or you get your money back.
- Working with cities to set consistent deadlines for housing permit applications, so each application gets a decision quickly instead of sitting for months, or even years, without a decision.
- Create a standardized permitting form so cities and builders can reduce paperwork while maintaining local control.
- Work to secure federal rewards for cities created by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , which creates a $200 million-per-year Housing Innovation Fund for communities that measurably increase their housing supply.
## Cut red tape by streamlining building codes and removing costly mandates.
- Work with cities to remove mandates and redundant requirements that raise construction costs.
## Put vacant state land to work.
- Use state-owned surplus property and vacant office sites in towns and cities across the state, releasing suitable parcels for housing. Build on vacant land the state already owns to lower costs, while conserving our public lands and parks.
- Publish a searchable statewide inventory of surplus public land suitable for housing to ensure Minnesota is ahead of the new federal requirement that communities receiving Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds publish databases of undeveloped public land.
## Reward communities that choose to build.
- Create a Minnesota Pro-Housing Incentive that rewards cities that want to build housing. Cities that voluntarily agree to build more housing, including renovating vacant commercial buildings, should be rewarded when applying for state funding.
- Align state incentives with the new federal BUILD Now performance incentives to encourage communities that receive CDBG funds to use them for new affordable housing construction, which the new law allows for the first time.
## Incentivize private investment in housing developments.
- Make the State Housing Tax Credit permanent to incentivize private investment in housing and rental buildings across Minnesota.
## 2. More Housing in Rural Communities
Rural and small-town Minnesota faces a unique version of the housing shortage: high infrastructure costs, aging housing stock, and limited access to assistance. For years, major employers and communities in Greater Minnesota have struggled to house the people they need to grow and thrive. In 20 rural counties, more than half of renters spend more than 30% of their income on rent.
As Senator, Amy Klobuchar worked with Senators Jerry Moran (R-KS) and Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) to change the law to give nonprofits and local and tribal governments that develop building sites for families more flexibility to get rural projects built.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will support rural communities that want to build more homes, including by incentivizing the conversion of vacant commercial space into housing and the rehabilitation of abandoned residential properties. This is just one part of Amy Klobuchar’s plan to strengthen economic development in rural Minnesota. Read Amy Klobuchar’s full plan to expand Minnesota’s rural economy here: AmyKlobuchar.com/rural .
## Lower the cost of building in small towns.
- Launch a Rural Housing Loan Fund, a low-interest revolving pool to help rural developers cover the high infrastructure costs of building in small towns.
- Use the State Housing Tax Credit to incentivize private investment in housing and rental construction across Greater Minnesota.
- Convert vacant commercial space to housing, helping small-town owners turn empty storefronts and upper floors into apartments, with incentives for renovation.
- Rehabilitate vacant and abandoned buildings by creating competitive grants.
- Protect rural renters by directing Minnesota Housing to help owners access the Department of Agriculture ’ s (USDA) rural rental assistance that they can now receive after their mortgage ends.
## 3. Make Owning a Manufactured Home More Affordable
Factory-built starter homes are one of the most affordable paths to homeownership. Amy Klobuchar’s family knows this personally – her husband, John, grew up in a manufactured home until he was in the 6th grade. Treating manufactured housing fairly expands supply at the price point Minnesotans most need. Manufactured home owners often face unique burdens: many families own their home while renting the land beneath it, which leaves them exposed when a private equity owner raises fees, neglects upkeep, or sells the land. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work to support owners of manufactured homes and remove barriers that undermine them.
## Support owners of manufactured homes from deception.
- Guarantee residents a real opportunity to purchase the land under their own homes. Require park owners to give notice before a sale and a genuine window for residents to make an offer to buy the land in their communities. C ompete for the reauthorized federal PRICE grants, extended for seven years under the new 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , to repair and preserve manufactured homes and communities, including helping residents purchase their parks.
- Protect residents from deceptive, hidden charges and poor maintenance. Shield manufactured home park residents from unpredictable and excessive increases in their lot fees, and eliminate the practice of compounding late fees and multiple increases within a single year. Require park owners to provide transparent, itemized billing for all services and guarantee residents secure payment methods.
## Remove barriers to building manufactured homes.
- Incentivize the removal of burdensome rules that effectively ban the addition of high-quality manufactured housing. Update state codes and certify compliance with new federal standards.
- Promote new Federal Housing Administration (FHA) financing established by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , which families can use to buy manufactured homes.
## 4. Support Renters and Stop Rip-Offs
Predatory pricing is driving up housing costs. Large out-of-state companies – from tech companies to private equity firms – are coordinating prices, using complicated corporate ownership schemes, and targeting neighborhoods to raise costs. Sometimes, these practices are outright illegal.
The state of Minnesota has sued the software company RealPage and six large corporate landlords for using algorithms to illegally fix rent prices. The lawsuit was filed in coordination with the federal government and a bipartisan group of nine other states. As Senator, Amy Klobuchar called for an investigation into RealPage in 2022, held hearings into these issues, and introduced a bill to take on price fixing using algorithms. We must do more to take on price fixing and predatory practices that increase housing costs for everyone.
## Protect renters from unfair discrimination.
- Adopt commonsense protections that already exist in many states that ban landlords from rejecting renters just because they use housing vouchers.
## Ban price-fixing algorithms.
- Stop companies from using shared algorithms to coordinate rent prices. As Senator, Amy Klobuchar introduced a bill to take on price fixing using algorithms, and as Governor she will work to ban this practice in Minnesota.
## Require transparency and fair treatment from institutional landlords.
- Make large institutional landlords report acquisitions and rent increases and release this information in a public database so Minnesotans can see whether they are pushing up local rents. In addition, the Senator supports the Senate-passed ROAD to Housing Act , which puts caps on the number of homes owned by large institutional landlords.
## 5. Help Minnesotans Buy Homes and Afford Rent
While assistance exists for families struggling to afford a home or pay their rent, too often it is impossible for them to access it. Homebuyers must often submit identical information across multiple agencies. Renters must navigate a patchwork of programs and forms. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will make it easier for Minnesotans to access existing housing assistance so families can afford their homes and stay in their homes.
Amy Klobuchar is committed to making government accountable to Minnesotans – and turning the page on a bureaucracy that forces people to jump through hoops to get the support they need.
## Simplify the path to home ownership.
- Combine state down-payment assistance, local grants, and federal assistance into a single application, and provide counseling to help homebuyers access this assistance.
- Bring small-dollar mortgages to Minnesota, facilitated by the FHA’s new pilot program for mortgages under $100,000 established by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act .
## Make rental assistance easy to find and more accessible.
- Create a No Wrong Door network so any Minnesotan who contacts a state agency or local provider is connected to the rental assistance they qualify for, rather than forcing renters to navigate a patchwork of programs.
- Preserve existing affordable housing, so the rental homes taxpayers have already funded stay affordable.
## 6. Prevent and Reduce Homelessness
As Senator, Amy Klobuchar has led efforts to reduce homelessness, authoring bipartisan legislation that was signed into law to support homeless veterans; cosponsoring the Homeless Children and Youth Act to help homeless youth; and pressing HUD to provide more housing security to teens and young adults aging out of foster care.
As Governor, she will reduce homelessness by connecting people to the housing and services they need, lowering housing costs, and expanding on bipartisan work to end veteran and student homelessness.
Prevent and reduce homelessness by connecting people to support.
- End the cycle of homelessness by establishing a No Wrong Door network that connects people to housing and supportive services through a single point of contact.
- Simplify the Local Affordable Housing Aid (LAHA) and Statewide Affordable Housing Aid (SAHA) programs by streamlining administrative requirements, clarifying eligible uses, and reducing duplicative reporting.
Continue work to end veteran homelessness.
- Expand the Homeless Veteran Registry that lets state agencies, counties, and partners coordinate to ensure housing for every veteran.
- Leverage Klobuchar’s bipartisan law to connect veterans in rural and underserved areas to the federal vouchers and case management they have earned by serving our country.
Prevent student homelessness.
- Launch a statewide initiative to end homelessness among Minnesota’s students and their families, building on the success of Minnesota’s bipartisan work to end veteran homelessness.
- Identify students who are homeless or at risk of homelessness and connect them to help. Coordinate support across agencies, including early identification of students experiencing housing instability, targeting resources to students and families who qualify for housing assistance, and building partnerships among state agencies, local governments, school districts, community partners, and families.

pages.title: Prepare Minnesota’s Workforce for the Future - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Prepare Minnesota’s Workforce for the Future
Amy Klobuchar knows there are many paths to success. As governor, she’ll make sure Minnesotans can get the skills they need to build a good life here at home.
Watch in a new tab
“In Minnesota, anybody willing to work should have a path to success – whether that’s through high-quality education, apprenticeships, workforce programs, or earning a credential or degree.
“Because a strong economy depends on preparing Minnesotans for the future and giving them pathways to a good job.
If given the opportunity to serve as your Governor, I will be laser-focused on getting Minnesotans the skills they need to build a good life here at home.”
## A plan to prepare Minnesota’s workforce for the future by:
- Build real on-ramps to good jobs. Expand apprenticeships and earn-while-you-learn pipelines for Minnesotans at any stage in their career, especially in teaching, health care, public safety, and the trades.
- Raise academic achievement across Minnesota. Expand the use of evidence-based curricula that have been proven to work in districts across the country to increase reading and math skills, so more kids graduate ready to succeed.
- Open the doors to college and credentials . Expand community college and one-to-four-year degree pathways that connect directly to in-demand careers.
Amy Klobuchar knows there are many paths to success. Her grandpa was an iron ore miner who never graduated from high school, but saved money in a coffee can to send her dad to college. Her dad graduated from Minnesota North College – Vermilion Campus, then known as Ely Junior College, and earned his journalism degree from the University of Minnesota before going on to be a sports reporter and a newspaper columnist. Her mom was a teacher who taught second grade until she was 70-years-old. Senator Klobuchar knows from experience that various credentials, apprenticeships, or college degrees can open up doors to good careers across Minnesota.
As governor, she’ll make sure Minnesotans can get the skills they need to build a good life here at home. Because a strong economy depends on preparing Minnesotans through high-quality education, increasing student achievement, apprenticeships, workforce programs for high-demand jobs, one-to-four-year degrees, and beyond. She’ll work with employers to create credentials that give students the skills they actually need to get a job. That’s how we support an innovation economy and stay competitive in emerging and growing industries like health care and biotech, precision agriculture, and advanced manufacturing.
## 1. Build On-Ramps to Good Jobs with Apprenticeships and Workforce Training
As our U.S. Senator, Amy Klobuchar has worked across the aisle to expand pathways to good jobs. She led the bipartisan Freedom to Invest in Tomorrow’s Workforce Act , signed into law last year, to allow families to use 529 savings accounts to pay for skills training, credentialing, and apprenticeships. And she has long championed her bipartisan American Apprenticeship Act to provide tuition assistance for workers in registered apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs. She knows these programs work, and as governor, she will expand them in Minnesota.
## Use apprenticeships and new workforce pathways to increase opportunities.
- Strengthen registered apprenticeships by adding 10,000 apprenticeship and skills training opportunities, roughly doubling the number of registered apprentices. Build on the success of apprenticeships in the trades – like for electricians and plumbers – by bringing the Minnesota Apprenticeship Initiative to additional industries like biotech, health care, advanced manufacturing, and precision agriculture. Connect high school students directly to emerging and high-demand careers in cybersecurity, technology, and nursing, as well as the trades – which is especially important right now in the age of AI.
- Expand educators, health care, and public safety professional pipelines. Broaden recruitment of educators, health care, and public safety professionals, including teachers, nurses, doctors, med techs, and police officers by waiving initial application fees to reduce the financial burden on recent graduates and new professionals. Expand alternative pathways and streamline credentialing so promising workers, including graduates in other fields, can transition more easily into classrooms and clinical settings.
## Make it easier to navigate skills training and match with a job.
- Align workforce and higher education. Combine skills training, apprenticeships, and workforce programs from various state agencies into one place so Minnesotans can find and access these opportunities. Build on what works instead of adding duplication to give students, job seekers, and employers clear pathways and accountable results.
- Strengthen career navigation and job matching. Give workers and employers better tools to connect and pair training with supportive services, especially childcare and housing, that too often keep people from finishing a program or taking a job. Leverage regional Workforce Development Boards to ensure strategies are informed and responsive to the needs of local communities and employers.
## Respond to the current and future needs of workers and employers.
- Launch a Minnesota “Future of Work” initiative with incentives, credentials, and public-private partnerships that help businesses train their employees in emerging fields such as cybersecurity, tech management, and advanced robotics.
- Launch a public-private Skilled Workers and Trades Fund . Create a dedicated, public-private fund for debt-free, short-term training in the trades, health care, education, emergency services, public safety and other in-demand occupations. Built alongside employers, this fund can prepare our workforce for a changing job landscape as a result of AI.
## 2. Raise Academic Achievement Across Minnesota
Amy Klobuchar believes in using the best ideas – because Minnesota’s kids deserve excellence, and our economy needs a strong workforce. As both a mom and the daughter of a teacher who taught second grade until she was 70-years-old, Amy Klobuchar knows the importance of education and student achievement. As governor, she will use proven evidence-based approaches to raise student achievement, reduce racial and economic disparities in education, and push real improvement in our schools.
## Use proven approaches to raise student achievement.
- Improve reading and math skills. Ensure proven, evidence-based curriculum in elementary classrooms, and give teachers and parents the training and materials to deliver reading and math excellence. Instruction must follow what the research shows works to lift student achievement and reduce disparities in education. This is similar to the evidence-based approaches taken in other states, which are using phonics curriculum, high-quality instructional materials, and teacher training to improve reading and math scores. Require parent-teacher meetings for students who are behind in reading and math.
- Give children the extra help they need to succeed with reading and math tutoring. When students fall behind in reading or math, they shouldn’t be left to struggle. Partner with schools to provide regular, small-group tutoring that helps students build confidence, catch up, and stay on track. Research shows that targeted tutoring is one of the most effective ways to accelerate learning and close opportunity gaps. Establish a Minnesota Summer Reads Initiative to support summer reading programming through public-private partnerships.
- Advance Minnesota STEM education. Partner with our world-class tech, manufacturing, and medical employers to expand science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education, with mentorships, internships, and curriculum aligned to the jobs being created in Minnesota.
- Make sure our educators have the resources they need to succeed. Continue to strongly fund our schools and work to make health care more affordable for school personnel.
- Keep students on task. Ban cell phones and other personal mobile devices in K-12 classrooms , with narrow exceptions for genuine emergencies and medical needs, which more than 35 states already do. Work with school districts to set evidence-based limits on screen time – the amount of time students spend on tablets and computers – in the classroom.
- Boost attendance to ensure kids are learning. Work with schools, parents, and communities to track real-time daily attendance so that kids are at school and learning. Expect schools to identify attendance concerns early, communicate promptly with families, and intervene before attendance problems become academic problems. Send automated alerts to families as soon as students show early signs of chronic absence.
- Prevent student homelessness. Launch a statewide initiative to end homelessness among Minnesota’s students and their families, building on the success of Minnesota’s bipartisan work to end veteran homelessness. Identify students who are homeless or at risk of homelessness and connect them to help – so students are housed and ready to learn. Read more about Amy Klobuchar’s plan to lower housing costs and prevent student homelessness here: AmyKlobuchar.com/housing.
## Build clear, early pathways from school to opportunity.
- Start career exploration and work-based learning earlier. Partner with businesses to begin career exploration in middle school, and expand high-quality Career and Technical Education (CTE), internships, youth apprenticeships, and job-based learning so students see a direct line from school to a good job.
- Open more doors to advanced curricula. Establish statewide expectations that schools automatically offer enrollment in advanced courses for students who demonstrate proficiency for those classes.
## 3. Open Doors to College and Credential Pathways
A one-to-four-year degree and beyond are pathways that provide options to students and expand our workforce. Amy Klobuchar has advocated for more federal funding for community, technical, and tribal college programs. As governor, Klobuchar will keep working to expand affordable access to all Minnesota colleges, including community and technical colleges, so costs never keep a Minnesotan from a credential that leads to a good job.
## Expand college and credential pathways to the workforce.
- Create partnerships between local employers, community colleges, and public and private colleges and universities. Partner community colleges with local employers who are competing in the global economy to design curricula and credentials for high-demand jobs that exist right now, in fields such as clean energy, advanced manufacturing, AI, and health care, so training aligns directly with local hiring needs. Work with the University of Minnesota and Minnesota State Colleges and Universities to align programs with regional employers and simplify the transfer from community colleges into four-year degrees.
- Launch Employer Training Incentives. Implement a tiered tax credit for small- to medium-sized businesses that supports training, allowing businesses to offset some of the cost for recognized certifications.
- Expand three-year degrees. Support accelerated higher education pathways modeled after successful initiatives like the Rochester NXT GEN MED program. By partnering with employers and utilizing year-round learning, students can enter the workforce a year sooner with less debt.
## Help high school students start working toward a credential or college.
- Continue dual enrollment and early college. Pair high school with college-level coursework aligned with high-demand skills, so students can leave high school with real momentum toward a credential or degree.
- Automatically notify high school seniors of Direct Admissions. Notify graduating seniors of the Minnesota public and private colleges that they have qualified for based on their GPA.
