pages.title: Take on Crime and Support Public Safety - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Take on Crime and Support Public Safety
“Minnesotans should feel safe, and our law enforcement should have the support they need to keep Minnesotans safe and put criminals behind bars. As Governor, keeping Minnesotans safe is the first commitment I will make every single day.
“For eight years I ran the biggest prosecutor’s office in Minnesota, where we prosecuted major gang members and other violent criminals, and sent them to prison.
In the Senate, I’ve worked across party lines to pass public safety legislation, including more support for law enforcement and additional resources to hire and train officers.
As Governor, I will have zero tolerance for crime. I will assist local police departments to hire and retain more officers; take on organized crime and gang violence; and make sure our police officers and first responders have the resources they need to do their jobs.”
Amy Klobuchar ran the biggest prosecutor’s office in Minnesota for eight years as Hennepin County Attorney, where she made combating violent crime a top priority while strengthening the office’s focus on fraud, financial crimes, and corruption. She knows firsthand the vital role law enforcement and public safety officers play in keeping Minnesotans safe – and the importance of giving them the resources, training, and support they need to do their jobs.
In the U.S. Senate, Klobuchar has continued to make public safety a top priority, working across party lines to pass legislation to increase support for local law enforcement and combat fraud, human trafficking, and the fentanyl epidemic. She has led efforts to reauthorize the COPS Hiring Program, which has brought in over $35 million to Minnesota and helped state and local law enforcement hire more than 140,000 police officers nationwide, and has secured nearly $50 million in funding for law enforcement in Minnesota in just the last four years. Klobuchar has supported efforts to prevent violent extremism at home, including by strengthening partnerships between law enforcement and local communities to disrupt terrorist recruitment, and between federal, state, and local law enforcement to investigate and stop acts of terrorism. She worked to successfully pass the bipartisan STOP School Violence Act with Senator Orrin Hatch (R–UT) to invest in school security infrastructure, evidence-based violence prevention training, and anonymous threat-reporting systems to stop violence before it happens. Klobuchar has secured multiple grants for the security of religious institutions, protecting churches, synagogues, and mosques across the state, including most recently $2.6 million for Annunciation Catholic School. She has also taken action to stop drug smuggling, leading the Synthetics Trafficking & Overdose Prevention (STOP) Act , which was signed into law to prevent fentanyl shipments from being smuggled into the U.S. through the mail, and successfully worked to pass laws to declare international fentanyl trafficking a national emergency and sanction transnational criminal organizations. And Klobuchar worked to pass the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act , the first gun violence prevention law in nearly 30 years, including provisions based on a bill she led to prevent abusive dating partners convicted of domestic violence from purchasing a firearm.
Klobuchar has received national awards for her work on behalf of law enforcement, including the Major County Sheriffs of America’s Legislator of the Year award with House Speaker Mike Johnson (R–LA) in 2026, the Fraternal Order of Police National President’s Advocacy Award in 2025, and the National Association of Police Organizations’ Legislative Award for Outstanding Support for America’s Law Enforcement in 2024. As Hennepin County Attorney, her office was one of only nine jurisdictions nationwide to be recognized as a community prosecution leadership site by President Bush’s Department of Justice, and she was honored by Mothers Against Drunk Driving for successfully advocating for passage of Minnesota’s first felony DWI law.
Minnesotans should feel safe in their homes, schools, workplaces, and places of worship. Law enforcement should have the support they need to keep Minnesotans safe and put criminals behind bars, and our criminal justice system must be focused on public safety and based on justice. As she announced alongside law enforcement leaders in White Bear Lake, as Governor, Klobuchar will:
- Take on organized crime and gang violence. Local, state, and federal law enforcement officers must work together to address violent crime and gun violence. Klobuchar will establish a Regional Gang Violence Task Force – led by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA) in coordination with law enforcement from Anoka, Carver, Dakota, Hennepin, Ramsey, Scott, and Washington counties as well as Minneapolis, St. Paul, Metro Transit, and college and university police departments – which will target gangs and organized criminals committing violent crime, with clear oversight and accountability. She will also build up programs like the Violent Crime Enforcement Teams (VCETs), provide additional resources for investigations, operations, and prosecutions, and focus state resources on solving crimes across the state in order to hold criminals accountable.
- Assist local police departments to hire and retain more officers. Klobuchar knows that too many agencies are short on law enforcement personnel. As Governor, she will assist local police departments to put more cops on the street by establishing state grants for cities and counties to hire and retain more police officers – and by waiving initial application fees, expanding alternative pathways, and streamlining credentialing so future law enforcement personnel from other fields can transition into public safety careers. She will ensure officers receive the pay and benefits that reflect the difficulties of their jobs.
- Provide Minnesota state and local law enforcement with the resources they need to do their jobs through state, federal, and other funding sources. Klobuchar has long championed the needs of Minnesota’s law enforcement as Hennepin County Attorney and U.S. Senator. As Governor, she will provide law enforcement agencies with the equipment, technology, and training they need to keep communities safe, including for counterterrorism operations, and she will increase the capacity of the BCA for forensic laboratories, investigators, crime-gun intelligence, and regional investigative capacity, including cyber.
- Strengthen community partnerships to prevent threats — including terrorism — before they materialize. Threats against schools, places of worship, public servants, and community institutions are rising, as Minnesota tragically experienced with the shootings at Annunciation Catholic Church. Klobuchar will build on statewide threat-assessment capacity at the BCA, working with schools, local police, election officials, and community organizations to investigate credible threats quickly and stop violence before it happens. She will strengthen partnerships between law enforcement and the communities they serve through community policing and improved training. Klobuchar will expand security resources for houses of worship and nonprofit organizations facing threats and strengthen efforts to investigate and prosecute hate crimes.
- Root out fraud and hold fraudsters and scammers accountable. Klobuchar will root out fraud with a top-to-bottom audit of state government, stop fraud before it starts by vetting grants and contracts before state funds are awarded, ensure in-person inspections and unannounced visits, and strengthen criminal penalties for stealing from taxpayers. Read Klobuchar’s full plan to take on fraud here: AmyKlobuchar.com/accountable . Building on her work in the Senate to protect victims of scams and fight scams targeting seniors, Klobuchar will expand the cybercrime capabilities at the BCA by hiring more digital forensic experts who can crack phones and trace stolen money. She will also strengthen coordination among law enforcement, financial institutions, and aging-services providers to identify scams.
- Ensure sentencing reflects the severity of a crime. Klobuchar believes there must be consequences for people who commit crimes, and she will work with county attorneys and law enforcement so that penalties match the seriousness of the offense.
- Protect critical infrastructure and be ready when emergencies hit. Cyberattacks on critical infrastructure are growing – in recent years, cyberattacks on Minnesota’s cities, water systems, schools, and hospitals have shut down services and exposed people’s private data. Klobuchar will create a statewide cyber response team that will bring together the BCA, state and local emergency management officials, and the growing and necessary cyber expertise of the Minnesota National Guard to coordinate with federal and private sector cybersecurity experts.
- Protect people from online exploitation and digital threats. Building on her leadership in the U.S. Senate to make the digital world safer, including her work with Senator Ted Cruz (R–TX) to pass the TAKE IT DOWN Act that criminalized the publication of non-consensual intimate imagery and required platforms to take them down, Klobuchar will ensure Minnesota law enforcement has the dedicated resources to combat and avert threats people face online. As part of that work, she will expand the Minnesota Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and make social media platforms actively cooperate with state law enforcement to identify and remove predators and illicit drug dealers targeting minors.
- Fight drug crimes. Too many people are caught in a vicious cycle of addiction, criminal activity, incarceration, and re-entry. Building on her leadership in the Senate, Klobuchar will strengthen coordination among state, local, and federal law enforcement agencies to take on drug-trafficking networks and hold gang members and those profiting from addiction accountable. She will target the networks moving fentanyl, methamphetamine, and other dangerous synthetic drugs through Minnesota, and improve technology and investigative resources for identifying and intercepting illicit narcotics, including dangerous drugs sold through social media and other online platforms.
- Expand mental health access. Klobuchar will work to build the mental health workforce, including dedicated mental health counselors and social workers, and will work to add psychiatric bed capacity, with a specific focus on kids, building on the 2025 bonding investment. She will work to restore and expand the school-linked mental health grants so kids and their parents can get help in school. Klobuchar will also direct the Commerce Department to enforce equal coverage for mental and physical health, so insurance covers mental health and addiction care like the health care it is, and will work to fully fund Minnesota’s mobile crisis response so that in a mental health emergency, help comes where it is needed.
- Support survivors of sexual assault and domestic violence. Klobuchar will work with counties to establish regional Family Justice Centers, building on Hennepin County’s Domestic Abuse Service Center, which Klobuchar strengthened as County Attorney and has supported as Senator. These centers are places where survivors of domestic and sexual violence can get legal help, counseling, housing support, and law enforcement in one place. She will make sure sexual assault kits are tested quickly, clear the remaining backlog, and expand access to forensic exams and victim advocates, with the assistance of the BCA where necessary.
- Prevent gun violence. Klobuchar will prioritize keeping guns away from people who should not have them while also protecting due process and the rights of the many law-abiding gun owners in Minnesota. She will sign the gun safety package that passed the Minnesota Senate to strengthen safe storage standards, ban assault weapons, and improve school security.

pages.title: Expand Minnesota’s Rural and Agricultural Economy - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Expand Minnesota’s Rural and Agricultural Economy
Amy Klobuchar knows one-size-fits-all solutions don’t work for rural communities.
Watch in a new tab
“Kids who grow up in rural Minnesota should be able to stay in rural Minnesota — but right now, too many can’t.
“As Governor, it will be my priority to expand our rural economy by opening up markets, making it easier for farmers to grow and produce more products, and helping families afford housing, health care, and child care.
I will find common ground and deliver real results for Greater Minnesota.”
## A plan to expand Minnesota’s rural and agricultural economy.
- Expand Minnesota’s rural economy by working with businesses and farmers to grow and produce more products, find new markets, invent things, and export to the world.
- Help families live and thrive in Greater Minnesota with more housing, affordable child care, health care, and educational opportunities.
- Keep rural Minnesota competitive and connected to markets, schools, and government with good broadband, infrastructure, and workable supply chains.
- Keep the farm safety net strong during difficult economic times.
As our U.S. Senator, Klobuchar has repeatedly reached across the aisle to deliver for rural Minnesota and our farmers and ranchers – working to open new markets for rural businesses, expand markets for E15, promote sustainable aviation fuel, and champion biomanufacturing. The Agriculture Committee was the first committee she asked to be on in the Senate, and as a member and current lead Ranking Member of the committee, she’s worked to pass three bipartisan farm bills into law and is currently working on a fourth.
Senator Klobuchar’s Lieutenant Governor running mate, Ben Schierer, former Mayor of Fergus Falls, worked to revitalize the town’s riverfront and bring local businesses back downtown. He started two successful businesses and he currently works with the West Central Initiative, a regional nonprofit dedicated to economic development.
Klobuchar and Schierer know that one-size-fits-all solutions don’t work for rural communities. Together they will make it easier for farmers to grow and produce more products, work with rural Minnesotans to find new markets, and support Minnesotans who are inventing things and exporting to the world. They’ll protect rural health care and support rural hospitals at risk of closing by protecting their 340B discount from efforts to restrict it, lower housing costs by working with the private sector to build more homes, and create new apprenticeships and one- to four-year degree programs and beyond, so that Minnesotans can afford to live, work, and raise a family in rural Minnesota. Because kids who grow up in rural Minnesota should be able to stay in rural Minnesota.
## 1. Expand Minnesota’s Rural Economy
The current federal across-the-board tariffs, volatile input costs, and cuts to rural health care have created major headwinds for our entire state, especially in rural Minnesota. These headwinds may well be constants, but they can’t be an excuse for not moving forward economically in Minnesota. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work with rural businesses and farmers to expand our rural economy by growing and producing more products, finding new markets, inventing things, and exporting to the world. That means partnering with rural businesses and helping them grow, expanding new markets and uses of products like biofuels, building local fertilizer production, supporting local food infrastructure, launching a Minnesota Innovation Network to cultivate new ideas across our state, and lowering the cost of farming. This plan has a particular focus on agriculture, with more to come as Klobuchar will outline plans for other economic sectors in the future.
This builds on Amy Klobuchar’s work in the U.S. Senate, where she has repeatedly reached across the aisle to deliver for rural Minnesota – teaming up with Senator John Hoeven (R-ND) to help rural businesses break into new international markets, working with Senator Deb Fischer (R-NE) to make E15 available year-round to support farmers and bring down fuel costs, advancing the bipartisan Farm to Fly Act with Senator Jerry Moran (R-KS) to expand sustainable aviation fuel and open new markets for farmers, and championing biomanufacturing to turn Minnesota crops into the products of the future. The Agriculture Committee was the first committee Klobuchar asked to be on in the Senate and as a member of the committee and current Ranking Member, she has worked with her colleagues to pass three bipartisan farm bills into law and is working on a fourth. And, as a senior member of the Senate Commerce Committee, she has put a major focus on workforce training, energy development, rural exports, and tourism in Greater Minnesota.
Klobuchar’s running mate, former Fergus Falls Mayor Ben Schierer, has extensive experience in rural economic development. As mayor, he worked to revitalize the Fergus Falls riverfront and bring local businesses back downtown. A former small business owner, he currently works with the West Central Initiative, a regional nonprofit dedicated to economic development.
## Expand rural Minnesota businesses.
- Increase markets for rural businesses. Partner with manufacturers, medical employers, and other businesses across Greater Minnesota to help them expand markets and grow. Work with the U.S. Small Business Administration, the federal Foreign Commercial Service, the Minnesota Trade Office (MTO) within the Department of Employment and Economic Development (DEED), and the IRRRB, to open new domestic and international markets for rural businesses and recruit new businesses in Greater Minnesota. This builds on Senator Klobuchar’s bipartisan legislative work with Senator John Hoeven (R-ND) to help small-town and rural businesses reach international markets and grow exports.
- Connect rural businesses to international markets. Make sure rural interests are included in any efforts to recruit and expand business opportunities with other countries. Put a special emphasis on export training for rural and small businesses, including farmers, ranchers, manufacturers, and innovators.
- Cut red tape for rural businesses. Give rural employers timely, predictable answers from state government so they can plan, expand, and build; pair the comprehensive permitting review and “One-Stop Shop” enrollment portal with firm response timelines and a single point of contact for a clear yes-or-no on permits, licenses, and land, without lowering health, safety, or environmental standards. Work with the Minnesota Chamber of Commerce, Enterprise Minnesota, and the trades to streamline permitting and encourage expansions, relocations, and startups.
- Expand access to state land for local development. Create a clear process for cities to acquire state-owned and tax-forfeited land for housing, commercial, and industrial development.
- Promote and expand tourism across our state. Promote rural Minnesota, including our parks and trails, agritourism, farm-to-table restaurants, breweries, museums, music venues, theaters, and – to mention a few – iconic sites like Bemidji’s Paul Bunyan and Babe the Blue Ox, Ironworld, Redhead Mountain Bike Park, the Central Lakes Region, Lake Superior, multiple river attractions, Mississippi River cruises, Tribal historic sites, and the world’s only SPAM Museum through Explore Minnesota. As a long-time lead of the bipartisan Senate Travel and Tourism Caucus and the lead author of multiple pieces of passed legislation on tourism, Senator Klobuchar will have a unique perspective on how to expand tourism in our state.
## Establish a Minnesota Innovation Network.
- Launch a Minnesota Innovation Network. Build a coordinated statewide system connecting Minnesota businesses across our state to universities, research centers, and incubators, as well as agencies and nonprofits like the IRRRB, AURI, and nonprofit development organizations. Create hubs in advanced manufacturing, energy, health care, and agriculture so that good ideas everywhere have a shot of becoming reality. Build on University of Minnesota research and outreach centers to research, develop, and scale technologies that make Minnesota farms and other rural businesses more profitable and resilient.
## Expand markets for Minnesota products.
- Make Minnesota the leader of the Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) industry. As the co-chair of the bipartisan U.S. Senate SAF Caucus, Senator Klobuchar has been an advocate for extending the 45Z clean fuel tax credit. Use the Minnesota SAF Production Credit as well as federal incentives to expand existing and attract new companies that will convert Minnesota-grown feedstocks into low-carbon jet fuel. Partner with major airlines at MSP Airport and feedstock processing facilities to make Minnesota a primary supplier for the sustainable-flight market and a new value-added stream for grain farmers.
- Grow bio-based manufacturing from Minnesota crops . Turn corn, soybeans, sugar beets, and their byproducts into higher-value bio-based products such as bioplastics and packaging, biochemicals, adhesives, and building materials. Apply a state purchasing preference for bio-based goods (building on the federal BioPreferred model), and connect growers and processors with the University of Minnesota, the Minnesota Innovation Network, and the Agricultural Utilization Research Institute to scale processing and add value to farm products in the state.
- Support biofuel production and new innovations that turn agricultural products like corn and soybeans into high-demand energy products.
- Grow Minnesota’s hemp industry . Create local jobs and new markets for farmers by increasing the use of industrial hemp and continuing safe regulation of hemp-derived recreational products. Direct MnDOT and state agencies to use bio-based (hemp-fiber) materials when they meet specs (e.g., erosion-control), creating stable in-state industrial hemp demand.
- Support sustainable practices by expanding incentives for precision agriculture, helping farmers apply inputs more precisely, saving money and protecting soil and water, with priority for projects that partner with innovation hubs. Expand voluntary, incentive-based programs that help farmers deliver ecosystem services, such as Minnesota’s soil-health equipment grants.
## Strengthen local food processing and infrastructure.
- Expand local and regional meat processing , creating new opportunities for farmers to market their products. Build on successes in meat processing to build more capacity across other product types.
- Strengthen the food supply chain with regional food hubs, warehouses where small farmers aggregate product for sale to hospitals, universities, and other public institutions, bridging the gap between a family farm and a large institution. Expand support for local farmers markets and increase institutional purchases of local food for schools, child-care centers, and hospitals through Minnesota Grown and Farm to School.
- Support Minnesota Grown to help producers brand and market local products.
## Lower the cost of farming.
- Lower costs for farmers and make farming easier. Expand the farm equipment sales-tax exemption to include fencing and grain-bin equipment, protect full first-year tax deductions for major farm equipment and machinery purchases, and update state programs so farms can access the resources meant for them.
- Build local fertilizer production and storage to create price stability for farmers by backing efforts to manufacture key inputs, including green ammonia, using renewable energy.
- Expand on-farm energy , supporting the development of on-farm solar, wind, and methane digesters.
## 2. Help Families Live and Thrive in Greater Minnesota
Kids who grow up in rural Minnesota should be able to stay in rural Minnesota – but right now, too many can’t. Employers struggle to recruit workers who can’t always find a place to live. Parents can’t take or keep jobs when there’s no child care nearby. And families won’t put down roots in communities where they can’t access health care – yet rural hospitals and clinics are at risk of closing because of new Trump administration cuts. Amy Klobuchar knows that one-size-fits-all solutions don’t work for rural communities, and she will work to close these gaps: building more homes, expanding child care options, protecting rural health care, creating new opportunities for apprenticeships and one- to four-year degree programs and beyond in everything from health care to hospitality to agriculture to mining and manufacturing, and supporting beginning farmers so that Minnesotans can afford to live, work, and raise a family in rural Minnesota.
## Lower rural housing costs.
- Lower rural housing costs. Work with the private sector to build more homes in rural areas by giving local developers the capital, incentives, and tools to build by launching a Rural Housing Loan Fund and making the State Housing Tax Credit permanent. Work with rural communities to develop and implement comprehensive housing plans using resources from the bipartisan legislation that Klobuchar wrote and became law as part of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act . Put underused buildings and land back to work, rehabilitate vacant and abandoned buildings, and use state-owned surplus property for housing. Read more about Amy Klobuchar’s plan for housing here: AmyKlobuchar.com/housing .
## Strengthen rural health care access.
- Recognize that one size does not fit all for health care. Stabilize critical access hospitals and clinics in Greater Minnesota by supporting and prioritizing modernization and upgrading infrastructure. Create a workforce pipeline by recruiting and training doctors, nurses, and medical technicians specifically for underserved rural areas. Support rural hospitals at risk of closing by protecting their 340B discount from efforts to restrict it. Lower prescription drug costs by leveraging the state’s purchasing power to negotiate directly with manufacturers and pass the savings on to patients.
## Increase access to affordable child care in rural communities.
- Expand rural child care by building on the great examples that already exist in rural Minnesota, from Luverne to the Iron Range, from Austin to Warroad, including expanding existing child care providers and supporting innovative models of care such as child care “pods.” Expedite state training and retention resources for communities with the most acute child care shortages, and help small child care providers reduce overhead while preventing fraud and waste with access to a child care operations hub.
## Prepare Minnesota’s rural workforce for the future.
- Build real on-ramps to good jobs by adding 10,000 apprenticeship and skills training opportunities, especially in teaching, health care, public safety, and the trades. Raise academic achievement across Minnesota using evidence-based reading and math curricula that have been proven to work in districts across the country – including in states such as Mississippi and Alabama – to increase reading and math skills. Keep students on task by banning cell phones in K–12 classrooms and work with school districts on screen time limits. Open the doors to college and credentials by expanding community college and one- to four-year degree pathways that connect directly to in-demand careers. Read Klobuchar’s full plan to expand Minnesota’s workforce here: AmyKlobuchar.com/workforce .
## Recruit talent and residents to Greater Minnesota.
- Build on the Explore Minnesota for Business that attracts new residents and workers to rural communities.
## Support beginning farmers.
- Coordinate resources for them and strengthening FarmLink. Provide a single point of contact to help new farmers navigate federal grants and loans, conservation programs, and state funding, while ensuring that farmers can count on programs like Minnesota’s Beginning Farmer Tax Credit. Match retiring farmers with new producers who can continue to work the land, including offering state-backed good-faith mediation to facilitate long-term leases or land transfers without costly legal fees.
## Advocate for immigration reform at the federal level.
- Our farms, dairies, and processing plants can’t run without workers, and a broken federal immigration system is holding Minnesota’s rural economy back in many sectors, including farming. Amy Klobuchar has led bipartisan efforts in the Senate to fix it. She’ll keep pushing for reforms that give farmers and employers a stable, legal workforce and the certainty they need to plan and grow. This is a federal responsibility, and she won’t stop working until we get it done.
## 3. Keep Rural Minnesota Competitive and Connected
Rural Minnesota’s economic strength depends on whether its people and businesses can get online, get their goods to market, and get a fair deal. Too many rural communities are still waiting for reliable broadband, watching roads and bridges deteriorate, and navigating a maze of government programs. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work to keep rural Minnesota competitive and connected – to markets, schools, and government – with good broadband, infrastructure, and workable supply chains. That means finishing the job on universal broadband; modernizing rural roads, bridges, and transportation infrastructure, including ports; making it easier for farmers and small businesses to access the programs they need; and fighting for fair prices for rural consumers and grocers alike.
## Complete the rural broadband buildout.
- Fully fund the Border-to-Border Broadband program by maximizing federal broadband (BEAD) funding secured by Senator Klobuchar to reach every corner of our state.
## Modernize rural roads, bridges, rail, ports, airports, and water systems.
- This includes always improving the excellent rail and port infrastructure that carries Iron Range iron ore, agricultural, and other products to the Port of Duluth and out to market. Use project bundling to combine multiple small bridge and road repairs into single contracts, cutting paperwork and overhead, and attracting more competitive private bids.
## Make government work for rural Minnesota.
- That means establishing a “One-Stop Shop” Enrollment Portal where farmers can apply for state (RIM) grants all at once to cut down on paperwork while preventing fraud. It also includes comprehensive permitting review so rural businesses can count on timely, predictable decisions to plan and complete projects, without lowering standards. And it means helping counties administer food assistance by combining and consolidating SNAP administrative functions and upgrading technology to reduce costs and paperwork, improving the program for Minnesotans and rural grocers.
## 4. Keep the Farm Safety Net Strong
While Minnesota continues to be the 6th-largest agricultural producer in the country, generating $100 billion each year and supporting nearly 400,000 jobs, our farmers are being squeezed from every direction at once. Nationally, farm bankruptcies have reached a five-year high and twice as many Minnesota farmers are using our state’s Farmer-Lender Mediation Program to stave off bankruptcy. They deserve a governor who has their back. As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will work to keep the agriculture safety net strong during difficult economic times. That includes expanding low-interest emergency loans for farmers facing market volatility, bolstering Minnesota’s veterinary response to animal disease outbreaks, strengthening farmer-lender mediation, and protecting the biosecurity programs that keep Minnesota’s livestock producers in business.
As our U.S. Senator, Amy Klobuchar has long led bipartisan efforts to strengthen the farm safety net, having worked to pass three farm bills into law and creating new U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) animal disease programs. With Senator John Cornyn (R-TX), she authored the Animal Disease and Disaster Prevention, Surveillance, and Rapid Response Act , passed in the 2018 Farm Bill, to create three programs, including a stockpile of foot-and-mouth disease vaccines. As lead Ranking Member on the Senate Agriculture Committee, she has continued to press the USDA on threats such as the avian flu and New World screwworm.
## Broaden the Rural Finance Authority.
- Offer more no-interest and low-interest loans for farmers facing extreme market volatility, trade disruptions, disease outbreaks, and weather. Expand the existing Disaster Recovery Loan framework to allow criteria beyond physical weather damage to qualify for loans and ensure growers can count on loans upon a confirmed avian flu detection.
## Expand the number of Minnesota veterinarians.
- Work with the Veterinary Reserve Corps, a network of private-sector veterinarians trained by the state to mobilize immediately during a suspected animal disease outbreak. Senator Klobuchar founded the bipartisan Senate Veterinary Medicine Caucus with Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS).
## Strengthen farmer-lender mediation.
- Help farmers facing bankruptcy or other financial stress reach an agreement with their lender, keep farming, and have mental health support.
## Protect Minnesota’s livestock producers.
- Expand and make permanent the AGRI Protect biosecurity grants and raise the per-farm cap so producers can afford barn-scale upgrades. Minnesota is the nation’s top turkey state, and avian flu has hit hard, with roughly 1.2 million commercial birds lost in 2025, with new outbreaks this year. Higher caps also help unlock federal indemnity now that audits are required before restocking.

pages.title: Support Conservation and Outdoor Recreation - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Support Conservation and Outdoor Recreation
“Like most Minnesotans, I grew up in a family that values the outdoors.
“Hunting, fishing, and outdoor recreation are a big part of Minnesota’s heritage but they must also be our future.
As Governor I’ll protect our land, water, and wildlife habitats so the next generations can continue to enjoy them.”
Amy Klobuchar is committed to preserving Minnesota’s natural resources and protecting the environment. Klobuchar grew up in a family that valued the outdoors, with a grandfather who was an avid hunter, a dad who was a mountain climber, bicyclist, and winter sports enthusiast, and a mom who loved to fish and hike.
In the U.S. Senate, Amy Klobuchar championed policies protecting Minnesota’s lands and waters. She played a key role in passing landmark 2022 legislation that made a historic investment in protecting our environment and cosponsored the Great American Outdoors Act , which became law and funds the Land and Water Conservation Fund. She authored the Upper Mississippi River Basin Protection Act and the bipartisan Local Water Protection Act to reduce pollution. She also serves as vice-chair of the Senate Great Lakes Task Force and supported the bipartisan Recovering America’s Wildlife Act to invest in state and Tribal fish and wildlife conservation. As lead Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, Klobuchar worked to advance the largest package of public lands bills out of the Committee in decades and is working to pass it into law.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will protect Minnesota’s natural resources, from lakes and wetlands to forests and farmland. She knows we all share a responsibility to pass on the Minnesota way of life to future generations through conservation and smart policies that allow outdoor recreation, fishing, and hunting to thrive. She will promote strategies that protect public lands and wildlife habitat, preserve farmland, reduce fires and flooding, and keep our state’s air and water clean. Klobuchar’s plan will:
- Protect Minnesota’s lands and waters by continuing support for the Clean Water, Land and Legacy Amendment.
- Support hunters, anglers, and outdoor recreation by strengthening habitat partnerships.
- Protect Minnesota’s wildlife with research funding and science-based policies.
- Expand the outdoor economy by investing in trails, water and land access, forests, and the travel destinations that depend on them.
- Prepare Minnesota for floods, storms, and fires by improving local readiness, strengthening the coordination of state programs, and bringing federal dollars home.
## 1. Protect Our Lands and Waters
Minnesotans have voted across party lines to protect the state’s lands and waters, from the Clean Water, Land and Legacy Amendment to the lottery-funded Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund. Amy Klobuchar strongly supported the Legacy Amendment and in the U.S. Senate she has secured federal funding for habitat and restoration projects across Minnesota and worked with Republican Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota to protect and enhance the federal conservation programs that keep working lands healthy. As Governor, she will protect what those Minnesota voters built. She will lay the groundwork to extend the Legacy Amendment before it sunsets, keep conservation funds invested in real, on-the-ground projects, and make drinking water safer in communities across the state.
Protect our lands, waters, and habitats.
- Extend the Clean Water, Land and Legacy Constitutional Amendment and continue to champion the work of the Outdoor Heritage Council. Amy Klobuchar was a strong and vocal supporter of the landmark Legacy Amendment when it was on the ballot in 2008. A s Governor, she will set the groundwork to extend it before it sunsets, protecting the fund that has invested more than $4 billion in parks, habitat, and clean water. She will champion the work of the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, keeping it intact, independent, and citizen-led. Minnesotans can see first-hand the results of the Legacy Amendment funding, as well as federal funding secured by Klobuchar, in projects like the restoration of Marsh Lake on the Minnesota River, where Ducks Unlimited spent more than a decade working to bring back a 5,100-acre shallow lake that once held 80,000 migrating mallards. This project also reconnected the Pomme de Terre River to its historic channel and opened a fishway for native fish. Minnesotans can see this work in the Worthington Wells wildlife management areas, which protect the drinking water of the city of Worthington. And they can see it in habitat restoration across the Red River Valley that is reducing the risk of flooding for landowners and entire communities. From the beginning, the Legacy Amendment has also supported Minnesota’s arts and cultural heritage, and Klobuchar will keep the fund’s arts and cultural work strong alongside its conservation mission, including projects that help communities preserve historic spaces and revitalize downtowns.
- Keep the Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund working for the outdoors. Minnesotans renewed the lottery-funded ENRTF with 77% support, dedicating 40% of state lottery proceeds to the outdoors through 2050. Amy Klobuchar will make sure those dollars are spent the way voters intended: on real, on-the-ground projects.
- Renew state parks and public lands by reducing the DNR ’ s deferred-maintenance backlog. As Governor, Klobuchar will work to build new DNR projects, from bridges to campgrounds, with climate-resilient, flood-mitigation standards when possible, so parks stay open and safe through floods.
- Fight for Minnesota’s conservation programs in Washington. Minnesota’s farmers and ranchers depend on federal conservation programs like the Conservation Reserve Program, the Conservation Stewardship Program, and the Environmental Quality Incentives Program to keep their working lands healthy and productive. Amy Klobuchar has long worked with Republican Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota to strengthen and expand these programs, and to ensure that the offices farmers count on are open and staffed. As Governor, she will continue this advocacy so that Minnesota farmers and ranchers who want to participate in these programs can access them and get the on-the-ground support they need.
- Support sustainable farming practices. Klobuchar will expand incentives for precision agriculture, helping farmers apply inputs more precisely, saving money and protecting soil and water. As Governor, she will work to expand voluntary incentive-based programs aimed at enhancing conservation, such as Minnesota’s soil-health equipment grants. Read more about Amy Klobuchar’s plan for the rural and agricultural community here: AmyKlobuchar.com/rural.
- Stand up for Minnesota’s public lands. Public lands belong to the people who use them. When Congress moved to strip protections from the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness and other federal lands through an unprecedented use of a procedural mechanism, Klobuchar voted no and warned it would have far-reaching consequences for public lands across the country. As Governor, she will oppose efforts to shrink the public lands and waters Minnesotans depend on, and she will work with partners like Pheasants Forever, Ducks Unlimited, and Minnesota’s land trusts to expand access to public lands.
Invest in safe drinking water .
- Make drinking water safer in communities across the state. As Governor, Klobuchar will work to improve aging water infrastructure and deploy Water Quality Technical Strike Teams to give small towns and local governments the engineering expertise to design runoff mitigation.
- Put water dollars into real projects. As Governor, Klobuchar will support the state’s Clean Water Fund dollars going to on-the-ground work that will have long-term, durable benefits for the state. She will pair state clean-water dollars with federal USDA conservation programs, including the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program.
## 2. Support Hunters, Anglers, and Outdoor Recreation
Hunting, fishing, and outdoor recreation are a big part of Minnesota’s heritage, and they are part of Amy Klobuchar’s own family’s heritage, too. In the U.S. Senate, she cosponsored the bipartisan Sportsmen’s Act to increase hunting, fishing, and recreational shooting access for sportsmen and women, and worked to expand the “open fields” program that creates public hunting and fishing opportunities on private land. As Governor, she will build on that work by opening more land to public access, strengthening habitat partnerships, putting more Department of Natural Resources (DNR) staff in the field, and recruiting the next generation of outdoor enthusiasts.
- Expand access to public lands. In the U.S. Senate, Amy Klobuchar worked to expand access to public lands for hunting, fishing, and outdoor recreation. She passed the bipartisan federal Sportsmen’s Act into law and led the reauthorization of the Voluntary Public Access and Habitat Incentive Program, the federal fund behind state walk-in programs, which was endorsed by Pheasants Forever, Ducks Unlimited, and the National Wild Turkey Federation. As Governor, she will continue that work, including by expanding Minnesota’s Walk-In Access program, which compensates private landowners who voluntarily open their land to hunters.
- Strengthen habitat partnerships. As Governor, Klobuchar will partner with land trusts and sportsmen’s groups such as Pheasants Forever and Ducks Unlimited, as well as Minnesota’s land trusts, and build on her federal partnership work. She will push state agencies out of their silos so habitat, clean-water, and flood-mitigation dollars are targeted and leveraged together, the way the Worthington Wells partnership secured both wildlife habitat and a fix for the city’s drinking water.
- Rebuild the DNR’s presence in Greater Minnesota . As Governor, Klobuchar will put more staff in the field than in the office, reversing the decline in conservation officers, wildlife biologists, and fisheries staff based in Greater Minnesota. Klobuchar will strengthen Minnesota’s conservation workforce and ensure our natural resources are protected, our outdoor traditions continue, and communities have the expertise to manage healthy ecosystems.
- Recruit the next generation of outdoor enthusiasts. As Governor, Klobuchar will expand youth mentorship, outdoor education, school forest programs, and learn-to-fish and learn-to-hunt opportunities throughout the state.
## 3. Protect Minnesota’s Wildlife
Minnesota’s wildlife face real pressures, from the loss of wetland habitat to chronic wasting disease and invasive species. We need policies that preserve our wildlife habitats, open spaces, and farmlands. In the U.S. Senate, Amy Klobuchar led the fight for continued funding of the North American Wetlands Conservation Act, the public-private partnership that matches federal funds to protect and restore wetlands, and she authored the bipartisan provision that permanently closed the Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock to keep invasive carp from moving upstream into Minnesota’s lake country. As Governor, she will work to restore the wetland habitat that waterfowl depend on, support a science-driven response to chronic wasting disease with sustained funding for testing and research, and take on invasive species before they spread.
- Launch a Minnesota waterfowl recovery effort. As Governor, Klobuchar will work to restore and manage shallow lakes and wetlands, working with sportsmen’s groups and habitat partners to bring back the wetland habitat that ducks and duck hunting depend on. In the U.S. Senate, she led the fight for continued funding of the North American Wetlands Conservation Act , which protects and restores vital wetlands for migratory birds. She also strongly supports the Duck Stamp Program, which spotlights Minnesota artists while funding permanent waterfowl habitat protection. As Governor, she will launch a waterfowl recovery effort focused on restoring the conditions that let waterfowl populations recover .
- Take on aquatic invasive species. Klobuchar has long fought to protect Minnesota’s waterways from invasive species, including authoring the bipartisan 2014 provision that permanently closed the Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock to stop invasive carp. As Governor, she will finish the job by completing the invasive carp deterrent at Lock and Dam 5 to safeguard Minnesota’s outdoor heritage for future generations. She will also continue to focus on all invasive species that pose a threat to our waters.
- Take on chronic wasting disease and support wildlife health. As Governor, Klobuchar will support a science-driven response to chronic wasting disease, including sustained funding for testing, carcass disposal, and research. In the U.S. Senate, she pushed the Departments of Agriculture and Interior to provide resources to combat chronic wasting disease and passed legislation providing $70 million a year for chronic wasting disease research and management.
- Manage Minnesota’s wildlife. Klobuchar supports pragmatic wildlife management that meets the goals of the Endangered Species Act while keeping decisions about Minnesota’s wildlife in Minnesota. She has backed bipartisan wildlife conservation bills, including the Recovering America’s Wildlife Act . She has also supported bipartisan legislation to return gray wolf management to the states once populations recover, while maintaining the ability to relist wolves if populations decline.
## 4. Expand the Outdoor Economy
The outdoors have drawn people to Minnesota for generations. Whether it’s hunting or fishing, canoeing or kayaking, biking or hiking, outdoor recreation is a major economic engine supporting small businesses, resorts, and communities across the state. In the U.S. Senate, when the Recreational Trails Program was targeted for cuts, Amy Klobuchar rallied a bipartisan group of senators to protect the trails used by snowmobilers, off-highway motorcyclists, all-terrain vehicle riders, bicyclists, and cross-country skiers. As Governor, she will work with leaders of Minnesota’s outdoors economy to strengthen the trails, water access, forests, and habitat that this economy is built on to support communities across Minnesota.
- Strengthen Minnesota’s trail networks. As Governor, Klobuchar will support snowmobile, ATV, hiking, biking, and cross-country skiing trail networks in every way possible, including through the grant-in-aid club system. She will keep winter and motorized traditions strong across Greater Minnesota, and work with Minnesota’s recreational sports businesses, like Polaris and Arctic Cat. In the U.S. Senate, Klobuchar led the bipartisan effort to strengthen and fully fund the federal Recreational Trails Program that Minnesota’s trails rely on, and has worked extensively in Washington with the recreational sports industry.
- Improve public water access, including boat landings, fishing piers, and shore-fishing sites. Minnesotans deserve more places to launch a boat, cast a line, and get out on the water. As Governor, Klobuchar will build on the Get Out MORE state investment that modernized boating access and fisheries infrastructure, including expanding the network of shore-fishing sites and piers.
- Champion the outdoor economy. As Governor, Klobuchar will continue and expand the Outdoor Recreation Industry Partnership. She will bring in Explore Minnesota, private-sector members, and outdoor-gear research and development, so the outdoor economy that contributes over $10 billion a year to our state keeps growing.
- Keep Minnesota’s forests a strong economic pillar. Klobuchar will support sustainable timber harvests and forest-products jobs, protect peatlands, invest in wildfire resilience across northern Minnesota, and improve forest health and habitat. She will create a Forest Bio-Packaging and Innovation Initiative to leverage Minnesota’s forest biomass for wood-fiber packaging and bio-based materials. In the U.S. Senate, Klobuchar worked across the aisle to improve the State and Private Landscape Restoration Program, which funds projects that protect forests, reduce wildfire risk, and conserve wildlife habitat.
- Support Minnesota’s family resorts. As Governor, Klobuchar will work to keep Minnesota’s small resorts in local hands by building public-private partnerships that provide the expertise, resources, and investment to preserve these community anchors for generations to come.
- Give Minnesota sixth graders a “Passport to Minnesota.” As Governor, Klobuchar will work to provide a free one-year pass for sixth-grade students and their families to visit state parks, as well as participating museums and historic sites, paired with the sixth-grade Minnesota history curriculum.
- Make neighborhood sports affordable and available. As Governor, Klobuchar will keep taxpayer-funded fields and ice rinks, like those built through the James Metzen Mighty Ducks Act , open to the community by limiting overly exclusive private leases, and use state authority to keep Minnesota’s nation-leading community ownership of athletic facilities from being bought up by out-of-state, investor-owned enterprises.
## 5. Prepare Minnesota for Natural Disasters
Floods, storms, and wildfires cause serious damage across Minnesota, and we need to be ready when natural disasters strike. In the U.S. Senate, Amy Klobuchar led Minnesota’s federal delegation in advocating for federal disaster relief, secured provisions in the Water Resources Development Act to improve shoreline resiliency and flood protection, and pressed the federal government to ensure we have the resources and firefighters to protect against and fight wildfires in Minnesota. As Governor, she will strengthen disaster response, coordinate the state’s work, and keep bringing federal dollars home.
- Respond to floods and severe storms. As Governor, Klobuchar will strengthen flood mitigation and emergency preparedness, work with farmers on programs that reduce erosion, and aggressively pursue federal disaster and resilience funding. In the U.S. Senate, Klobuchar has led Minnesota’s federal delegation in advocating for federal disaster relief, including Army Corps of Engineers funding to build and rebuild multiple projects, USDA and EPA resilience grants, and funding through the Water Resources Development Act , and she will continue that work as Governor.
- Strengthen wildfire readiness in northern Minnesota. Northern Minnesota’s fire risk is rising, as evidenced by the 2026 far-reaching Boundary Waters Canoe Area fires. The June 2025 derecho in Bemidji is an example of a storm that left millions of downed trees, which increases the risk of fires for years to come. As U.S. Senator, Klobuchar has pressed the federal government to ensure it has the resources and firefighters to fight and prevent fires in Minnesota and across the country. She has also supported legislation to cut red tape, increase interagency coordination, and invest in community resilience. As Governor, Klobuchar will partner with local, Tribal, and federal governments on fuel reduction and community risk reduction; invest in the equipment, training, and staffing that local and volunteer fire departments need; strengthen mutual-aid agreements and regional emergency coordination; press the federal government to fund hazardous-fuels work on federal land in Minnesota; and support communities doing the defensible-space and evacuation planning that keeps people safe.
- Coordinate disaster resilience. As Governor, Klobuchar will consolidate and better coordinate the state’s overlapping climate-resilience entities. She will establish measurable goals for community preparedness, emergency planning, shelters, backup power, and recovery programs.

pages.title: Make Child Care More Affordable and Available - Amy Klobuchar for Governor
pages.text:
## Make Child Care More Affordable and Available
“Child care is essential for kids who need it to prepare for school, parents who can’t take a job if there is no one to watch their kids, and Minnesota’s economy.
“For too many Minnesota families, child care is not affordable or not available.
It can cost as much as a mortgage, and even when families can make the math make sense, they are often stuck for months on waiting lists.
As Governor, I will expand access to the quality, affordable child care that Minnesota families need.”
Minnesota families deserve child care that is safe, affordable, and high-quality. Amy Klobuchar has long fought for child care and early education, which are essential for Minnesota families and for Minnesota’s economy. Child care is where student achievement begins. Kids who arrive at kindergarten ready to learn do better in school and in the workforce, and high-quality child care delivers one of the strongest returns of any public investment. At the same time, parents cannot go to work and jobs go unfilled if there is no one to watch their kids. Families deserve more quality child care, and Klobuchar will deliver on that by increasing supply, lowering costs, and ensuring transparency and accountability.
In the Senate, Klobuchar has led bipartisan legislation to reduce child care shortages by expanding training for the child care workforce and has obtained funding for multiple projects to build and expand child care facilities throughout the state. She cosponsored federal legislation to expand child care by making it more affordable for children from birth to age five. And she has supported bipartisan legislation that was signed into law to reauthorize and improve Head Start. Klobuchar helped secure Minnesota’s Race to the Top – Early Learning Challenge grant, making Minnesota one of nine states to receive funding for children in need. And when the Trump administration froze funding for Head Start and child care programs across the country, threatening care for over 10,000 Minnesota children, Klobuchar and her colleagues successfully fought to restore access to those resources.
As Governor, Amy Klobuchar will make child care more affordable and more available across Minnesota. She will expand access to child care options – including in rural Minnesota, where there is much need – by training more child care workers, building more child care facilities, and cutting red tape and lowering overhead for small providers. She will support innovative models such as expanding existing day cares, building new ones, centers in existing schools and buildings previously used for schools, on-site work day cares, and child care “pods” – all while streamlining the support available for families. Klobuchar will have zero tolerance for child care fraud and will root it out and stop it before it starts.
Klobuchar’s plan to make child care more affordable and available:
- Expand affordable child care options and the child care workforce.
- Make child care more affordable for families.
- Increase transparency, eliminate fraud, and make sure every dollar goes to families who need it.
## 1. Expand Affordable Child Care Options and the Child Care Workforce
- Support innovative child care models. Build on the great examples that already exist, including building new child care facilities, as Brooklyn Park has; expanding existing child care providers; co-locating child care with senior living centers, as Burnsville and Warroad are doing; using underused buildings for child care, as Windom is doing with a former school; and supporting family child care networks and child care “pods” like those launched in Stevens County. These models are acutely needed in Greater Minnesota, and already exist from Luverne to the Iron Range and from Austin to Warroad. Read more about Amy Klobuchar’s plan to expand Minnesota’s rural economy at AmyKlobuchar.com/rural .
- Expand child care centers to increase supply, including by using underused buildings. Provide financing and assistance so providers can open or expand, including in former schools, unoccupied buildings, and other underused spaces. All over the state, cities and towns are turning empty and donated buildings into child care facilities, and the state should support those efforts.
- Expand the child care workforce. Recruit and train child care professionals, expand alternative pathways to child care jobs, and waive initial licensing and application fees to reduce the financial burden on new workers. Give child care workers and providers better tools to connect, so qualified Minnesotans can find work in the communities that need them. Provide consistent funding that creates stability for providers, and streamline and consolidate the dozens of separate workforce grants that currently exist across agencies. Read more about Amy Klobuchar’s plan to prepare Minnesota’s workforce for the future at AmyKlobuchar.com/workforce .
- Partner with employers to expand child care. Work with businesses, hospitals, nursing homes, and schools to open or expand child care centers that serve employees and surrounding residents. Work to expand grants for employers who help pay their workers’ child care costs, prioritizing small businesses and communities with severe shortages.
- Reduce overhead for small providers. Launch a child care operations hub that allows small and home-based providers to share a network for payroll, billing, and insurance, cutting red tape and costs while supporting child care workers. Streamline licensing and permitting and regularly review child care rules to make sure they are accomplishing their purpose without adding unnecessary costs or paperwork. Ensure requirements are reasonable, and work with local governments to standardize permitting for small and home-based providers while keeping safety standards high and taking action to end fraud.
## 2. Make Child Care More Affordable for Families
- Streamline child care aid into one easy-to-use program. Increase access to affordable child care by combining Minnesota’s two child care assistance programs – the Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP) and child care scholarships – into a single scholarship-style program with one application review, thorough vetting, and one website where parents can find open slots and apply.
- Deliver child care scholarships for more children. Minnesota lets parents choose child care through scholarships, which has encouraged providers to open and expand, including in child care deserts – but many more families who qualify could still benefit from the scholarship. Expand the scholarships so more families receive them, making child care more affordable for them. Work with the private, nonprofit, and public sectors to build a lasting funding partnership for child care.
- Advocate for federal funding for Minnesota. Continue fighting back against the Trump administration’s nationwide funding cuts to child care and Head Start, so Minnesota families and providers who qualify for support do not have it ripped out from under them.
## 3. Increase Transparency, Eliminate Fraud, and Make Sure Every Dollar Goes to Families Who Need It
- Zero tolerance for child care fraud – root it out and stop fraud before it starts. Transform state government across child care programs so every dollar goes to actual child care, not to services not delivered: root out fraud with a top-to-bottom audit of state agencies and by replacing decades-old computer systems; vet grants and contracts before state funds are awarded; stop fraud before it starts with in-person inspections and unannounced visits; create a “Do Not Pay” database to automatically block anyone convicted of fraud against state programs from receiving any grants and contracts; and establish a permanent ban for anyone convicted of fraud against state grants or contracts. Strengthen criminal penalties and extend the statute of limitations for fraud in all state programs, not just Medicaid. Read Amy Klobuchar’s full plan to make the government accountable and root out fraud at AmyKlobuchar.com/accountable .
- Increase transparency with clear goals for school readiness. Hold child care programs to a high standard – because that’s what Minnesota’s families deserve. Put down markers for what children should know and be able to do when they start school, measure progress every year, and report the results.

I’m kicking off a Northwest & Northern Minnesota rural tour.

They're working on moving overhead powerlines underground & improving reliability with the help of federal funding.

Places like this help showcase all that Northwest MN has to offer.

Last year they returned to independent ownership, they’re thriving, and they’re one of this region’s largest employers.
Great way to kick off our country’s 250th birthday: a visit to one of Minnesota's many innovators – Arctic Cat — here in Pennington County!

I met with local leaders about how Warren stepped up to address child care needs with the Little Sprouts Learning Center. When parents can’t find care, they can’t go to work, & local economies suffer. We must support local solutions like this.

At New Moon Coffeehouse in Baudette, I joined local leaders & volunteers ahead of their Walleye Fish Fry and July 4th celebrations — with so many visitors coming in to mark our nation’s 250th birthday & enjoy the outdoors! 🏕️🎇

Nothing like northwestern and northern Minnesota in the summer 🇺🇸 … with our friends in Canada 🇨🇦 right across the river!

Happy Independence Day, America! 🇺🇲

To all our veterans, service members, and military families – thank you. 🇺🇲
